details:
=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:251-256 | severity=critical | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, x-ai_grok-4_1-fast]
  PROBLEM: The gate sets SHOULD_RUN=false for any non-open PR, including merged PRs, so standalone review-blocked recovery never reaches the judge.
  WHY: This blocks the documented rerun-after-merge recovery path and leaves the follow-up issue uncreated.
- scripts/review_rb_judge.sh:522-545 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [x-ai_grok-4_1-fast]
  PROBLEM: The judge comment is posted before the merged-PR safety guard runs, so a refused action can still leave a comment implying the action was chosen.
  WHY: This creates a misleading audit trail because the refusal is only determined after the comment is already emitted.
- scripts/review_rb_judge.sh:526-549 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [x-ai_grok-4_1-fast]
  PROBLEM: The merged-PR safety guard exits without emitting judge_action=skip or judge_skip_reason=merged_pr_unsafe_action.
  WHY: Downstream workflow parsing cannot classify the refusal explicitly and sees an unknown failure instead of a skip.
- scripts/review_rb_judge.sh:636,683 | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m2_5]
  PROBLEM: The grep pattern still accepts the unreachable PR state merged even though GitHub REST returns only open or closed.
  WHY: This is dead code that misstates the API shape and can confuse maintainers.
- scripts/review_rb_judge.sh:799 | severity=low | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [x-ai_grok-4_1-fast]
  PROBLEM: The PR-state grep still accepts merged even though that state is never returned by the REST API.
  WHY: This is dead code and misleads readers about the allowed PR states.
- scripts/review_rb_judge.sh:860 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [x-ai_grok-4_1-fast]
  PROBLEM: The standalone gh pr merge --squash path does not bind the judged head SHA with --match-head-commit.
  WHY: A concurrent push can change HEAD between judging and merging, allowing unjudged code to land.
- scripts/review_rb_judge.sh:926-928 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, qwen_qwen3_6-plus]
  PROBLEM: The merge_with_followup merge command does not pass --match-head-commit.
  WHY: A push between judging and merging can change the PR head and invalidate the judged diff.
- scripts/review_rb_judge.sh:926-928 | severity=medium | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5]
  PROBLEM: The code treats gh pr merge --squash returning 0 as proof that the PR has actually landed, even in merge-queue repos.
  WHY: In merge-queue repos 0 can mean the PR was queued rather than merged, so the follow-up issue can be created for code that never lands.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:10127-10128 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [qwen_qwen3_6-plus]
  PROBLEM: The orchestrator refusal path sets REVIEW_BLOCKED_STATE_CHANGED=true but does not emit judge_action=skip or judge_skip_reason=missing_followup_details.
  WHY: Observability diverges from the standalone judge and the refusal cannot be classified cleanly downstream.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:10127-10128 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  PROBLEM: The orchestrator refusal path logs an error but sends no Telegram notification when follow-up details are missing.
  WHY: Operators monitoring Telegram can miss repeated refusals because the only signal is a workflow annotation.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:10130 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [x-ai_grok-4_1-fast]
  PROBLEM: The PR-state whitelist omits merged even though the surrounding logic treats merged PRs separately via PR_MERGED_NOW.
  WHY: The validation is functional but inconsistent and misleads maintainers about the allowed state set.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:10148 | severity=low | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, qwen_qwen3_6-plus, z-ai_glm-5]
  PROBLEM: _rb_mwf_sha is extracted from the PR JSON but never referenced anywhere.
  WHY: This is dead code and looks like an intended merge-safety hook that was never wired in.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:10148 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [x-ai_grok-4_1-fast]
  PROBLEM: The merge_with_followup branch skips the _pr_checks_completed gate used by the plain merge path.
  WHY: It can attempt a sync merge while checks are still running, unlike the standard merge flow.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:10158-10189 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, qwen_qwen3_6-plus]
  PROBLEM: The merge_with_followup branch skips the _pr_checks_completed gate used by the plain merge path.
  WHY: It can attempt a sync merge while checks are still running, unlike the standard merge flow.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:10169-10172 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [x-ai_grok-4_1-fast]
  PROBLEM: gh_retry wraps the merge command even though merge failures here are not transient.
  WHY: The retries burn backoff time before the warning path and delay recovery.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:10189-10191 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [qwen_qwen3_6-plus]
  PROBLEM: The merge_with_followup merge command does not pass --match-head-commit.
  WHY: A push between judging and merging can change the PR head and invalidate the judged diff.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:10189-10191 | severity=medium | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  PROBLEM: The code treats gh pr merge --squash returning 0 as proof that the PR has actually landed, even in merge-queue repos.
  WHY: In merge-queue repos 0 can mean the PR was queued rather than merged, so the follow-up issue can be created for code that never lands.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:2455 | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m2_5]
  PROBLEM: The PR-state whitelist still accepts the unreachable merged state even though GitHub REST never returns it.
  WHY: This is dead code in the orchestrator and misleads maintainers about the API shape.
- tests/test_review_rb_judge_label_propagation.py:663 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, x-ai_grok-4_1-fast]
  PROBLEM: The helper uses a bare list type annotation where the sibling helper uses list[str].
  WHY: This weakens static typing consistency, though runtime behavior is unaffected.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:10148 | severity=low | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: _rb_mwf_sha is extracted from the PR JSON but never used.
  WHY: The variable is dead code and looks like an intended merge-safety hook that was never wired in.
- scripts/review_rb_judge.sh:926-928; scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:10189-10191 | severity=medium | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: Both merge_with_followup paths treat gh pr merge --squash returning 0 as a definitive merge in merge-queue repos.
  WHY: In merge-queue repos the command can only queue the PR, so the follow-up issue may be created before anything lands.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:10127-10128 | severity=low | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The orchestrator merge_with_followup refusal path does not send a Telegram notification when follow-up details are missing.
  WHY: The ::error:: annotation is easy to miss, so repeated refusals can be invisible to operators watching Telegram.
=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
